newsitem.title: USA: BellSouth, IBM in Internet alliance.
newsitem.headline: BellSouth, IBM in Internet alliance.

text.p: BellSouth Corp and International Business Machines Corp have agreed to a strategic alliance for Internet and intranet services in the southeastern United States, the companies said Wednesday.

"Our agreement with IBM will enable BellSouth to provide our Internet services to more than 70 percent of our customer base region-wide," said John Robinson, president of BellSouth.net Inc. "This positions BellSouth to be the leading Internet service provider in the Southeast."
The companies plan to work together over the longer term to design, develop and deploy the Next Generation Internet Platform (NGIP).
The platform will accommodate emerging technologies like Asymmetrical Digital Subscriber Line (ADSL) and new technologies relating to enhanced speed, security and capabilities on the Internet.
BellSouth said it will use the IBM Global Network to extend its dial-up Internet services to an additional 30 markets in the Southeast this year.
The company currently offers BellSouth.net service for consumers and small businesses and Commerce-Link Internet and intranet services for larger businesses in 14 major markets.
Robinson said connecting through the IBM Global Network will allow BellSouth's Internet customers to access the Internet from more than 830 locations in 49 countries with a local telephone call.

Also as part of the pact, IBM said it plans to use BellSouth's suite of Commerce-Link services, which provide businesses with dial-up and dedicated Internet and intranet connections and value-added IP network services, for their customers in the Southeast.
